1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, wherein the non-native compartment is engineered to contain a heterologous enzyme not naturally present in the BMC compartment.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo and comprises at least one heterologous targeted enzyme not naturally associated with the BMC polypeptide.

3. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme that is heterologous to the BMC polypeptide.

4. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes, at least one of which is heterologous to the BMC polypeptide.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence and is heterologous to the BMC polypeptide.

6. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the BMC polypeptide comprises a Eut polypeptide and the non-native compartment further comprises at least one heterologous enzyme.

7. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 6 wherein the Eut polypeptide comprises a EutS polypeptide.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides and at least one heterologous enzyme not naturally present in the BMC compartment.

9. (Original) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different bacterial species.

10. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different BMC operons and the non-native compartment comprises at least one heterologous enzyme.

11. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein at least one BMC polypeptide comprises an affinity tag and the non-native compartment comprises at least one heterologous enzyme.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and at least one heterologous enzyme not naturally present in the BMC compartment, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and the heterologous enzyme, and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one BMC polypeptide and sequestering the heterologous enzyme.

13. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a bacterium and the heterologous enzyme is not naturally associated with the BMC polypeptide in the bacterium.

14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Enterobacteriaceae and the heterologous enzyme is from a different bacterial species.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 14 wherein the member of the family Enterobacteriaceae comprises E. coli and the heterologous enzyme is not naturally present in E. coli BMC compartments.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Shewanellaceae and the heterologous enzyme is heterologous to the Shewanellaceae BMC compartment.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a yeast and the polynucleotide encodes a heterologous BMC polypeptide not naturally present in yeast.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17 wherein the yeast comprises a member of the family Saccharomycetaceae and the BMC polypeptide is heterologous to the yeast.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 18 wherein the member of the family Saccharomycetaceae comprises Saccharomyces cerevisiae and the BMC polypeptide is not naturally present in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises an alga and the polynucleotide encodes a heterologous BMC polypeptide not naturally present in the alga.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, and at least one heterologous enzyme that is not naturally present in the BMC compartment and catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one heterologous enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a bioactive product and the enzyme is heterologous to the BMC compartment.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a drug or a drug precursor and the enzyme is heterologous to the BMC compartment.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a biofuel or a precursor of biofuel production and the enzyme is heterologous to the BMC compartment.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the at least one heterologous enzyme catalyzes a step in degrading or detoxifying a toxic substrate and is not naturally present in the BMC compartment.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 further comprising isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments comprising the heterologous enzyme.

27. (Original) The method of claim 26 wherein at least a portion of the non-native compartment comprise an affinity tag and isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments comprises contacting a sample comprising the non-native compartments with an affinity substrate having selective affinity for the affinity tag.

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of compartments, each comprising at least one heterologous enzyme not naturally present in the BMC compartment.
